Even if accounts associated with the device have been deleted - which is the case here, the  engine recognizes the device as having participated in those campaigns. This means that new users connected to the same device may be restricted from enrolling in additional campaigns. Please do not share these details with users. This is to prevent users from deleting their accounts and creating new ones to abuse the campaigns offered. If this is a targeted campaign offered to very limited number of users, then campaigns team should set the configuration as compensational to make sure that fraud rules will not prevent those specific group from ordering.

h3. 1. *Germany*

* *Relevant Laws & Directives*:
** EU Trademark Regulation (2017/1001)
** German Trademark Act (MarkenG)
** Trade Secrets Directive (2016/943)
** German Act on the Protection of Trade Secrets (GeschGehG)
* *Gap Identified*: No formal brand usage policy
* *Risk*: Unauthorized use or modification of registered trademarks
* *Mitigation*: Implement formal brand usage guidelines and pre-approval workflow for marketing assets.

h3. 2. *France*

* *Relevant Laws & Directives*:
** EU Copyright Directive (DSM) 2019/790
** French Intellectual Property Code (Code de la propriété intellectuelle)
** Trade Secrets Directive (2016/943)
* *Gap Identified*: Outdated copyright tracking
* *Risk*: Use of expired or unlicensed third-party content in advertising
* *Mitigation*: Introduce digital asset management (DAM) system to track copyright and licenses.

h3. 3. *Spain*

* *Relevant Laws & Directives*:
** Spanish Intellectual Property Law (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1996)
** EU Copyright Directive (DSM) 2019/790
** Trade Secrets Directive (2016/943)
* *Gap Identified*: No copyright approval workflow
* *Risk*: Infringement claims from unauthorized use of images, videos, or text
* *Mitigation*: Establish content approval workflows with copyright compliance checks.

h3. 4. *Italy*

* *Relevant Laws & Directives*:
** Italian Industrial Property Code (Codice della Proprietà Industriale)
** EU Trademark Regulation (2017/1001)
** Trade Secrets Directive (2016/943)
* *Gap Identified*: No trademark review process
* *Risk*: Misuse of third-party logos or slogans in campaigns
* *Mitigation*: Legal review of marketing materials involving third-party brands.

h3. 5. *Netherlands*

* *Relevant Laws & Directives*:
** Dutch Trade Secrets Act (Wet bescherming bedrijfsgeheimen)
** Trade Secrets Directive (2016/943)
** EU Trademark Regulation (2017/1001)
* *Gap Identified*: Lack of trade secret controls
* *Risk*: Loss or leakage of proprietary operational data or software
* *Mitigation*: Implement company-wide NDA policies and secure information storage protocols.

h3. 6. *Poland*

* *Relevant Laws & Directives*:
** Polish Industrial Property Law
** EU Trademark Regulation (2017/1001)
** Trade Secrets Directive (2016/943)
* *Gap Identified*: Inconsistent logo use
* *Risk*: Weak trademark protection, dilution of brand value
* *Mitigation*: Launch mandatory brand use training and asset repository.

h3. 7. *Romania*

* *Relevant Laws & Directives*:
** Law No. 84/1998 on Trademarks and Geographical Indications
** Law No. 11/1991 on combating unfair competition
** Trade Secrets Directive (2016/943)
* *Gap Identified*: No local IP policy
* *Risk*: Unclear IP compliance expectations among staff and contractors
* *Mitigation*: Roll out Romanian-localised IP policy and training.

h3. 8. *Portugal*

* *Relevant Laws & Directives*:
** Portuguese Code of Copyright and Related Rights
** EU Copyright Directive (DSM) 2019/790
** Trade Secrets Directive (2016/943)
* *Gap Identified*: No copyright checklist
* *Risk*: Accidental use of copyrighted content without attribution or license
* *Mitigation*: Provide teams with a copyright compliance checklist for daily operations.

h3. 9. *South Africa*

* *Relevant Laws & Directives*:
** Trade Marks Act 194 of 1993
** Copyright Act 98 of 1978
** Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) — relevant to confidentiality obligations
* *Gap Identified*: Minimal brand training
* *Risk*: Misuse of Bolt’s own trademarks and unawareness of third-party IP boundaries
* *Mitigation*: Develop online training modules focused on IP basics and brand usage.

h3. 10. *Thailand*

* *Relevant Laws & Directives*:
** Trade Secrets Act B.E. 2545 (2002)
** Copyright Act B.E. 2537 (1994), as amended
** Trademark Act B.E. 2534 (1991), as amended
* *Gap Identified*: Weak confidentiality protections
* *Risk*: High exposure to loss of proprietary data or business methods
* *Mitigation*: Enforce stricter contract clauses and secure data handling practices.

This is similar to if we had a recommendation that was rolled out and did not work, we would have to roll back.  Second point is the recommendation actually has about 9% increment in some hours which seems high given we are already priced higher than competition. Given our price drop was below -5%,  reverting would mean not much of an increase and would keep us competitive. For context, we do factor in competition pricing before pricing changes. It’s the reason the GM is recommending we hold on to reverting prices last week.

On the expected supply drop, I would keep it at max -10% as the trends are comparatively positive this year.

Hi team, 

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount. 


Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Cheers,
Marten

We could populate 3 data sources:

----

*Table 1: Daily Copilot Usage Summary*

* *Purpose:* Tracks overall daily Copilot activity and main feature usage.
* *Key Data Points (per day):*
** *Date:* The specific day of the metrics.
** *Total Active Users:* Count of users with any Copilot activity.
** *Total Engaged Users:* Count of users with significant Copilot interaction.
** *IDE Chat Users:* Users of chat within their code editor.
** *GitHub · Build and ship software on a single, collaborative platform* *Chat Users:* Users of chat on the GitHub website.
** *Pull Request Summary Users:* Users of Copilot for PR summaries.
** *Code Completion Users:* Users of Copilot for code suggestions.

----

*Table 2: Daily Copilot Usage by Editor*

* *Purpose:* Shows which code editors are used with Copilot daily and for what interactions.
* *Key Data Points (per day, per editor, per interaction type):*
** *Date:* The specific day of the metrics.
** *Editor Name:* The code editor used (e.g., "VS Code", "JetBrains").
** *Interaction Type:* How Copilot was used (e.g., "Code Completion", "Chat").
** *Number of Users:* Count of users for that specific editor and interaction.

----

*Table 3: Daily Copilot Usage by Programming Language*

* *Purpose:* Tracks which programming languages are most frequently used with Copilot's code completion feature each day.
* *Key Data Points (per day, per language):*
** *Date:* The specific day of the metrics.
** *Language Name:* The programming language used (e.g., "Python", "JavaScript", "Java").
** *Number of Users for Language:* Count of users who used Copilot for code completions in that specific language.

*Rolling mean vs loess*
Previously we used to have lowess for trend, now we are alternatively discussing rolling mean.
Both are languages to describe smoothening and extent of that smoothing.

Choosing between the two, it seems that language of rolling mean is just more comprehensible (the concept of window is clear)
-Argument for loess is that it is more resilient to outliers (and ideally we want our trend pattern without those – they are not part of process)- ==> You achieve very similar trends, just make the window wider

How smooth do we want our time series to be? 

* More Smoothened
** +()peaks about more long-term "trend" dynamic
* Less Smoothened
** (+) gives “more noise” (makes markets more realistic)
** (+/-) potentially includes variance related to our ads impact (might start correlating with ads, ideally we want our trend to exclude ads) – should not be a huge issue though (because we are modelling total trend, not Android and iOS separately), so effect (if is there) should go to both Android and iOS in the proportion of their split
** (+/-) potentially includes variance related to our tourist (but like in previous point, it will be split between Android and iOS according to their share.
** (+) includes outliers (but we are introducing the procedure to get rid of them on both modelling and simulations level)

Going with 7-day rolling mean for now

_In relation to your request regarding the suspension of your Bolt account, please note that irregular activities were detected on your account. The suspension involves suspicious account activities and orders._ 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* which you are entitled.

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*Your rights* 

 In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

Yours sincerely, 

Bolt

Hi [~accountid:641aac4f9d6383e32a32c047] 

As discussed on Slack, 

# From a pure 'GDPR' perspective, we are entitled to share Swedish employee data with other Bolt Group Companies, especially those in the EU and UK (which are deemed 'adequate' countries under EU Law)
# *However*, if local Swedish laws (particularly the Swedish Whistleblower Protection Act) set out restrictions on the sharing of whistleblower data between Bolt's Group Companies, then that is different and would operate as {{Local Law }}on top of the GDPR (which is a {{Regulation}}) i.e. the GDPR does not override local Member State laws.

I've researched the law in Sweden and what I've found is that:

# There is no _explicit_ prohibition on inter-company sharing in the Swedish Act. Rather, an exception is granted for Companies with less than 250 employees to share this information between their group of companies ([+Section 3 of Chapter 5 of the Act+|https://www.government.se/contentassets/4c12e7e33d43403ea34067bbd240a3a9/act-on-the-protection-of-persons-reporting-irregularities-2021_890.pdf]). However, the absence of this exception for companies with more than 250 employees is understood to introduce a restriction on Bolt.
# I've verified that Companies with more than 250 employees are not permitted to use the same reporting channels and procedures — see [+*2024 WLG Whistleblower Guide: Sweden*+|https://www.theworldlawgroup.com/membership/news/news-2024-wlg-whistleblower-guide-sweden]. I agree with the Swedish Law Agency's advise.
# The law itself doesn't actually refer to 'accessing' whistleblower data, but rather, the use of the same reporting channels and procedures. So, we need to verify that we are not allowed to grant access to [@nick.walker|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U07LHBPTEUS], for example, to local Swedish Whistleblower data, even if that data is maintained by the Local Swedish Team using their own reporting procedure/channel.

In short, if we wan't to comply with local requirements in Sweden, we should respect this rule. By breaching the local Swedish Whistleblower Law, we may in turn breach the GDPR as our other European Group Companies would not have a legal basis to process the data (i.e. because they weren't allowed to process it under the law). Breaching GDPR can have significant fines, as you're aware.

*Steps*:

* We need to consider how we can respect this rule (even partially), even if it means limiting the persons involved in handling Swedish Whistleblowing cases, and storing all that data locally in Sweden. Perhaps a call is necessary to brainstorm this point.
* It is worth looking into the 250 people threshold. The law isn't clear on whether it applies the local entity or the group and that's why a local written legal opinion should be obtained.
* We should probably get a written legal opinion on this topic. To clarify, there are 2 points for local counsel verification:
*# Is the restriction limited to the use of the same reporting channels and procedures, or does it also apply to the reported whistleblowing case data too?
*# Does the 250 people threshold apply to the local Swedish entity, or the Group company under which the Swedish entity is a subsidiary, or both?
* Depending on how we choose to proceed, we can update our Whistleblower Policy accordingly.

Hope that's clear!

* If it is not a court order, then we need to look on whether they mentioned a specific law that requires us to disclose the data. Have they cited any laws in their request?

query

{noformat}SELECT oo.id,
    DATE(oo.created) AS created,
    oo.state,
    rso.state AS billing_state,
    oo.target_id,
    u.status AS user_status,
    u.last_update AS user_deleted_at
FROM ng_public.subscription_marketplace_offer_order AS oo
    JOIN ng_public.user_user AS u
ON oo.target_id = u.id AND u.status in ('deleted', 'archived')
    JOIN ng_public.subscription_recurrent_subscription_order AS rso
    ON rso.external_id = oo.id
    AND rso.client_type = 'marketplace'
WHERE (oo.state IN ('active', 'grace_period')
   OR rso.state IN ('active', 'grace_period'))
  AND oo.state != 'cancellation_requested'
  AND rso.last_update < NOW() - INTERVAL '4' HOUR
  AND oo.last_update < NOW() - INTERVAL '4' HOUR;{noformat}

*_Objective:_*
 Compare the effectiveness of Guarantee and First-Time Rider (FTR) discount campaigns across key performance metrics aligned [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ajL8NWVOY4OS9yM4aMlGgif7b8iPvsp_IOFDDCYNG2k/edit?tab=t.0]
*_Key Findings:_*

* FTR discount outperforms Guarantees on bringing more 2x incremental riders and also improved incremental rides
* Both campaigns have almost identical weekly spend which could infer that the performance gap isn’t necessarily driven by investment differences
* Guarantees outperformed FTR on retention, delivering nearly 2x more incremental retained rides (250 vs 133), confirming earlier hypothesis
* At city-level, most metrics align with the aggregated view result, though Madrid, Gothenburg, Krakow, and Bucharest showed negative incremental impact from guarantees (detailed analysis [here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Km_xjbSQlCI13xYrVASZPIelhu04lJA8WIlKkkgB0Sc/edit?gid=1696388330#gid=1696388330])
* Results were cross-checked when only Guarantee campaign was live for few days in April to reduce bias from users exposed to both treatment and remained consistent

*_Suggested Next Step:_*
Tailor campaign strategy by city (e.g., keep both in equally performing cities or pause one in underperforming markets). That said, this remains a preliminary suggestion and we can continue to monitor and revisit once the campaign cycle concludes in June

*Summary of the issue:*

* The rider [reported|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/544701316] the driver’s discriminatory behavior during a ride via the app.
* Edinburgh Council requested us to share personal details of a complainant from a case that was reported [^DPA Request_ Mr Alfredo Iacovone - 526454 (1).pdf] . Council’s exact wording: _'I would like to request the complainer’s contact details to investigate the incident that BOLT received on 27/03/2025 regarding Mr Alfredo Iacovone refusing to take customers'_
* As per Edinburgh's request, we asked the complainant for their consent to share their name, phone number and email. However, the complainant then requested a copy of the original correspondence from Edinburgh City Council. Here is the full correspondence with the rider: [^Bolt Mail - Bolt - Consent required- S-884255 (41a2809d-b568-4696-8e69-c47f7b1139f8).pdf] 
* We denied to provide the above, as it contained details of the driver and the document was intended for Bolt not the complainant/rider.
* CS advised the rider that due to privacy reasons we cannot provide them with a copy of the request, however, they can contact Edinburgh council directly and provided them with name, surname, position and work email address of the Council’s officer who made the request.
* The rider replied that we contradict ourselves in our statements, because we claimed that we _couldn’t provide the council’s request due to “privacy,” yet you disclosed the council officer’s full name and email address without confirming their consent._ And continued with clarifying that they _did not ask for a summary but requested the original correspondence, which they are legally entitled to under Article 15 UK GDPR and refusing to provide it while continuing to act on it is unlawful. As well as requested that our correspondence with them must be signed by an individual not by CS team._
* CS then provided a copy paste of the email from the Council’s officer to Bolt stating that ‘In order to take this investigation any further can you please inform the complainer that she will need to contact either myself at [miguel.paredesbandres@edinburgh.gov.uk|mailto:miguel.paredesbandres@edinburgh.gov.uk] or [licensing.enforcement@edinburgh.gov.uk|mailto:licensing.enforcement@edinburgh.gov.uk] with the following information: date and time of the incident location description of the incident.’

* CS explained that the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data.

*# Confirm the council’s genuine request, based on their original email, without distortion *- explained above.*
*# Produce the full, unredacted original email from Edinburgh City Council (complete headers, timestamps, sender/recipient fields) in PDF or EML format *- they insist on this in every repky to the CS.*

Some of the learnings:


* The RGBA and HEX codes for text color from the Figma [+file+|https://dashboard-02.braze.eu/engagement/templates_and_media/email_templates/660bb12b05810f0061db0f3c/682b20bffaaeb8151906cec2] / [+Template+|https://dashboard-02.braze.eu/engagement/templates_and_media/email_templates/660bb12b05810f0061db0f3c/6790d38caebf6d008082d671] can’t be accurately replicated in Braze, Changing opacity is not supported using the Email Drag & Drop editor( for example , [+block+|https://dashboard-02.braze.eu/engagement/templates_and_media/content_blocks/660bb12b05810f0061db0f3c/682585015370f40067f3af4a]: rgba(0, 10, 7, 0.63) , the Hex code 000a07, not supporting opacity, hence the color we are getting in templates is different from original), what color should be used in such cases ?

In Spain, the obligation to provide information about the vehicle and the insurance company in case of an accident is regulated by the Royal Legislative Decree 8/2004, of October 29th, which approves the revised text of the Law on civil liability and insurance in the circulation of motor vehicles. This regulation establishes that every owner of a motor vehicle normally based in Spain must subscribe and maintain in force an insurance contract covering the civil liability derived from the circulation of the vehicle.

In addition, Article 2 of this law provides that insurance companies must send to the Ministry of Economy and Finance, through the Insurance Compensation Consortium, the necessary information on insurance contracts to control compliance with the obligation to insure. This information must include data that allows the persons involved in an accident to find out as soon as possible the circumstances relating to the insurance company that covers the civil liability of the vehicle.

Royal Decree 1507/2008, of September 12, 2008, which approves the Regulation on compulsory civil liability insurance in the circulation of motor vehicles, complements this legislation. It establishes that insurance companies must update and send information on insured vehicles, including license plates, make, model and policy number, to the Insurance Compensation Consortium. This body makes it easier to obtain this information for persons affected by accidents.

Therefore, in the event of an accident with a Bolt VTC vehicle, those affected have the right to access information about the vehicle and the insurer.

h2. *Product Prioritisation Procedure*

This procedure defines how compliance and regulatory risks are assessed, prioritised, and acted upon at Bolt. It provides a unified workflow combining legal and policy validation, risk scoring, and structured approvals, ensuring consistent, risk-informed decisions on product change requests are driven by regulatory needs.

 

h4. *A product request is raised:*

The business flags a (compliance-related) product gap (e.g. via #rides-compliance, #rides-safety), or Legal, Public Policy, and the Risk and Compliance teams identify or are informed of:

* new laws or regulations; or 
* changes in existing laws or regulations that will come into effect; or
* shifting regulatory landscape.

Central Operations to decide based on the nature of the slack message, whether to transition it to Jira or not for the prioritisation flow (generate a Jira ticket from the Slack message).

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*-> The product request flows into Jira.*
{panel}



h4. *Key info on the nature of the request is gathered via the prioritisation questions:*

Legal, Public Policy and Local Operations teams validate the regulatory basis of the request by completing a set of prioritisation questions to assess the urgency and legal exposure.

*_At this stage it should become clear whether the request is related to an internal process issue or needs development, before further steps are taken to assess the risk and prioritisation is conducted._*

*Types of requests Central Operations and Product might receive*

*Data sharing/Reporting*: government demands Bolt to share data about drivers and the order details
# Barcelona trip sharing
# Romania earnings sharing
# Czech Republic earnings sharing
# Azerbaijan data sharing with ANYA
# Sharing driving license & OH data in Malta
# *Supply document checks in government databases:*  government demands Bolt to validate a specific document externally
## TfL license validation
## CZ - business registry checks for drivers
## LV - license checks for drivers and cars
## PT - eligibility checks for drivers, cars, fleet companies
# *Process/requirement changes*
## Moving vehicle documents to vehicle entity
## Using hard blocks instead of suspensions
## Using 2 active partner accounts per person
## Duplicate rules changes
## Batch suspending stuff
## Validations through non-standard means
## Data collection & processing through non-standard means
## Internal fraud around service provider data & non-compliant OH’s
# *Product improvement requests*
## Comms messaging not perfect
## Expiry dates end in our system with 2038
## New metadata fields for documents
## Document system not flexible enough
## Delaying suspensions
# *Product development requests*
## Human review machine for blocks
## Bulk execution tooling
## Migrator tooling
## Vehicle verification tooling
# *Dependencies*
# *Services failing, e.g.* WASL integration fail

h4. *The following questionnaire should be answered:*

# Which market does this concern and does Bolt have an operating license in the respective country?
# Are there alternative solutions? YES/NO
# Is the request based on a *new national law?* YES/NO
# Is the request based on an *existing law*? YES/NO
# Does the legislation obligate *service providers*? YES/NO
# Does the legislation oblige *Bolt as a platform*? YES/NO
# When was the law announced?
## 12 months ago
## 6 months ago
## 3 months ago
# Has the *regulatory landscape changed suddenly*? YES/NO
# What happens if Bolt or supply do not adhere to the law within *the next 6 months*? 
## Fines from regulator *_> XXXXX Euros_*
## Loss of market share _(expressed as a sum not percentage)_ 
## Loss of supply _(expressed as a sum not percentage)_ 
## Loss of license
# Has the regulator announced enforcement of this law *within the next 6 months*? YES/NO
# Has the regulator announced *implementation of legislation* that would *complicate or negatively impact*  Bolt's operations in the market *within the next 6 months*? YES/NO
# Has Bolt become or is it likely that Bolt will become the subject of an investigation by the regulator *within the next 6 months*? YES/NO
# If Bolt's license is revoked, is there a risk that Bolt must immediately cease operations in the market *within the next 6 months*? YES/NO
# Please describe exactly what product change is requested.

*Prioritisation questions guidelines*

The general scoring logic is as follows:
* *YES: 1 point*
* *NO: 0 points*
Special circumstances to consider when scoring the request:
* *1 additional point* if the market *has* *an operator license*
* *1 additional point* if the market *is a business important market*
* Question 7 evaluation: 
** *1 point* for *a)*
** *0 points* if the answer is *b) or c)*
* Question 9 evaluation: 
** *0 points* if answer is *a)* and *height is* *_XXXXXXX Euros_*
** *1 point* if answer is *b) - d)*
The total of the questions determines the initial *Prioritisation Level:*
* *Priority 1: 8 or upwards:* The market is at risk within the next 6 months, if the initiative gets further postponed.
* *Priority 2: 6 - 7:* Postponing the initiative for 3-6 more months will not increase the existing market risk, however the initiative should be solved in the next 3-6 months.
* *Priority 3: 0 - 5:* Market is not at risk within the next 6 months, initiative can be postponed.
{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
Global de-risking and expansion initiatives should stay the highest priority. Global regulatory topics over local regulatory topics as global topics affect whole regions which means more countries are affected at the same time.
{panel}

h4. *A risk assessment is conducted:*

Product and Central Ops teams assign a *Risk Score* on the [+Risk Matrix+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VC5jjILT_vn6gEalO_Z8vD0MHo9vlzyTM2S5usM-z2Y/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.iu1bo4sruuto], based on: 

* [+Impact+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VC5jjILT_vn6gEalO_Z8vD0MHo9vlzyTM2S5usM-z2Y/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.s3p275w5151w] (regulatory, financial, reputational); and
* [+Likelihood+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VC5jjILT_vn6gEalO_Z8vD0MHo9vlzyTM2S5usM-z2Y/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.vo7w804bl6ih] (based on Bolt and competitor history and forecasts).

h4. *The product request is evaluated and prioritised:*

Using both the *Prioritisation Level* and *Risk Score*, the request is evaluated by Central Operations and Product, and a decision is made on how to treat the request.

{{Problem}} -> {{Validation}} -> {{Proposal}} to Product is made ->  {{Solution}} and {{Potential Timeline}} is agreed upon between Product, Central Operations, Public Policy, Legal etc -> _escalated_ _further_ *_conditionally_*_, based on impact_ (see bullet points below) -> {{Solution is Prioritised}}

* -> *approval is required* from VPs only if the problem (risk/compliance issue) is not mitigated and there is a fine or larger business impact (large % of supply lost, imprisonment of GMs), e.g. High/Significant risk.
* -> *approval is required* if strategic direction is needed and multiple solutions are possible, e.g. this can be discussed during monthly meetings where Product with Legal/PP/Privacy etc reviews incoming requests.
* -> *approval is not required* and a decision can be made by Central Operations and Product in collaboration if there is no fine/larger business impact.

h4. *A decision is made whether the product request is added to the roadmap:*

Stakeholder(s) approve or reject the proposal:

* If the request is *approved*, the request is actioned and monitored through delivery.
** If there is residual risk, it will be monitored continuously and the cadence will depend on the residual risk score.
* If the request is *denied*, the risk is documented, tracked, and monitored continuously. 
** If the request is denied with proposals to adjust the decision made or the order of prioritisation, then the request is sent back to the Central Operations and Product teams to revise, after which it will go through the final stakeholder review again.

Relevant teams are informed of the decision.

dLocal comment on this via email (Barbara Hackman, May 14, email to Kristiina Taube, Shuba and me :

dLocal does not fall in the support services definition, considering its role as a technological provider, the activities mentioned in the question happen in the partner’s platform.

# Article 3.17 defines “support services for entrusted collection and entrusted payment” as:


“Receiving and processing of electronic data, calculating collection and payment results, and cancelling collection and payment for customers with payment accounts, bank cards, and making payments to relevant parties.”
This implies operational control over transaction execution, involving handling actual payments, triggering settlement, and potentially acting on behalf of the bank or IPSP in executing fund transfers.

# dLocal VN’s Role is Passive and Backend-Oriented


By not being responsible for funds movement, dLocal has a supportive role to platform management - and not the execution of collection/payment services defined in Article 3.17. This lies with our partner, 9Pay. 

Because of these, the licensed intermediary payment service providers needs to be the one that execute core payment functions - as this will be done by 9Pay. 9Pay is a licensed party.

# Probably we would need to check metadata, especially for dates to see what has to change in our communication.

# *Daily company check-in* – every day, our system will look at all companies and decide whether they belong in *Activation* or *Reactivation*.
#  _Previously we did this only once at the very start._
# *User experience* – when a company qualifies, all of its users are put into the campaign for *30 (or 31) days*.

Example:

A user added on *June 1* stays in the campaign until *July 1*.

If their company qualifies again in July, that user gets another 30/31-day run starting from the new enrolment date.

Big picture

* *June 1 – August 31*: we run the company-check every day.
* Whenever a company meets the criteria, it (and therefore its users) gets dropped into the campaign.
* From the company perspective - they still get same campaign duration; but on the setup side the test and campaign start-end dates are close to 90.

* We have completed several improvements aimed at optimising response time when handling a larger number of providers.
* New Endpoint Introduced on Delivery Provider: /internal/v2/getPricingDataForProviders now serves pricing data using only providersMetadataCache, ensuring data is fetched exclusively from cache on the Provider side.

* New endpoints on Delivery Pricing Eater now accept full provider objects instead of just provider IDs. 
** Provider-related properties (traits, active delivery type, location, etc.) that were previously retrieved from Delivery Provider are now included directly in these new endpoints. 
** These changes aim to reduce response time in fee computation within Pricing Eater.
** All new endpoints are now integrated and fully used in: delivery-provider-search, delivery-eater-analytics, delivery-basket
** The previous endpoints have been removed from all three services, and corresponding tests have been updated.
* Code Improvements in Delivery Pricing Eater
** Replaced lodash with more performant alternatives: fast-deep-equal, custom cloning functions;
** Parallelised calls for prerequisites: targeting configs, provider pricing configs, dynamic multipliers, route distances.
** Parallelised calls to the database and cache where applicable when loading provider overrides, targeting configs and eater experiments data.
* Performance Results - *getDeliveryFeeForProviders* showed the most significant improvement (we will look at the 99th percentile) when delivery fees for multiple providers are requested:
** delivery-eater-analytics: response time reduced from ~2.35s to under 400ms (*~5x improvement*)
** delivery-provider-search: from ~500ms to under 260ms (*~2x improvement*)
** Average response time reduced from ~600ms to ~210ms (*~3x improvement*)

|*Absence/Time off plan*|*Description*|
|GBL Compassionate Leave|Flexible Plan, approver validates further eligibility and request duration|
|GBL Occupational Injury Sick Leave| |
|GBL - Other Leave|Accrue-as-you-go only for the listed countries in scope|
|GBL - Time off in Lieu|Balance will be added manually by Absence Partner before employee can request.|
|GBL Unpaid Leave|Accrue-as-you-go|
|POL Annual Leave|The default if TO Service date is blank will be 20 days
**For employees with < 10 years of TO service date:
20 days per year, counted in working days
*Employees with length of employment over 10 years based on TO service date in WD
26 days per year, counted in working days. The annual leave of employees who reach length of employment of at least 10 years, and will be able to show a proof of it accordingly to the PL Labour Law (study/employment  confirmation). 
**Non-regular employees with End Employment date will get their entitlement based on their End Employment Date
**Transition year rule: Calculate prorated additional days from 10 year Anniv till end of the year and give upfront at the beginning of balance year|
|POL Annual Leave on demand| |
|POL Blood Donation Time Off|Employees in Poland after donating blood are eligible for 2 days of time off to recover.|
|POL Child Birth Time Off|Mostly can be used by a partner of the person who's giving birth. An employee should provide a birth certificate.|
|POL Child Care|The right to 2 days off work or 16 hours to care for a healthy child. For this time, the employer pays remuneration for work. 
These 2 days are for a calendar year. Unused care for a healthy child is forfeited at the end of the year.|
|POL Child Care Sick Leave| |
|POL Family Care Sick Leave|Care allowance paid in case of a need to take personal care of a sick child over 14 years old or adult sick family member. 14 days per year.|
|POL Family Care Time off (Unpaid)|Everyone is eligible for this time off plan. No   attachments are required.|
|POL Force Majeure|Dismissal due to force majeure in urgent family matters caused by illness or accident - in total employee is eligible for 16 hours per year. As in the case of leave on demand, the employee can submit a request in any available form.|
|POL Sick Leave (Pregnancy)|The company pays the allowance for the first 33 days, which is covered by Social Security but no longer than up to 270 days. Plan is built as accrue as you go plan.|
|POL Wedding Time Off|Part of the occasional leave types in Poland, that employees can use for his/her wedding day and preparation for it. Employees are eligible for 1 day if they attend a wedding or 2 days if the employee is getting married.|

[~accountid:712020:807679ef-90df-4005-b1a4-e33c08b0cf30] Thanks for flagging. After reviewing Swiss data protection law and market practice, here’s my thoughts:

Yes, we can collect the “Strafregisterauszug” (criminal record extract) from drivers during onboarding and from existing drivers. This is considered sensitive personal data under Swiss law, but it is lawful to collect if we can demonstrate an overriding private interest, specifically, ensuring platform safety and maintaining public trust. This is consistent with what competitors like Uber do in Switzerland (don’t quote me on this - I’ve searched what’s available online on their website, but it seems like they do collect this data).

Uber requires Swiss drivers to submit a criminal record extract and relies on this same legal basis, coupled with clear privacy disclosures. Their privacy notice explains the rationale and aligns with public expectations around rider safety.

We will adopt the same approach. To support this, we will have to:

# Update our driver privacy notice globally to explicitly cover background checks and related data collection (this is already in the pipeline - no actions for you)
# Limit internal access to these documents and ensure secure storage - [~accountid:712020:807679ef-90df-4005-b1a4-e33c08b0cf30] please let me know where these are intended to be stored and who will have access to these docs
# Define a reasonable retention period and document our rationale - [~accountid:712020:807679ef-90df-4005-b1a4-e33c08b0cf30] please let me know if it’s possible to delete the docs sooner rather than later, and perhaps we can only store the fact that the driver has passed the check?

From a privacy perspective, no changes to the T&Cs are required. However, I’ll defer to [~accountid:712020:8fd75aa8-dcfb-42ad-93ab-53900ee4c301]  on whether there is any contractual or operational reason to adjust them.

Physical Android device set-up notes:

* connect device to Mac via USB and set connection to “file transfer”
* enable developer mode (from settings → about phone → tab a bunch of times on kernel version/os version) and thn allow app installation via USB

On a Xiaomi device I could not get past some security BS so I wasn’t able to install the apk directly as instructed in the food-delivery-courier-app project Readme.

Worked around that in the following way:

* run {{yarn android --device}} and select the physical device
* installation will fail, but the apk will be created in {{./android/app/build/outputs/apk/googleplay/debug/app-googleplay-debug.apk}}
* the phone should in theory show up in Finder, but not for me 🤷‍♂️ so I installed the Android File Transfer app, and used it to copy the apk on the phone
* manually install the apk on the phone

After installation, in order for the app to be able to connect to Metro and Reactotron, we have to forward some ports. So I did the following:

{noformat}yarn start
adb kill-server
adb reverse tcp:9090 tcp:9090
adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081{noformat}

Then restart the app and everything should work. If not, proceed to restart all components in various order and eventually it should work 🙃 



Bonus: if you want to open the {{android}} folder in Android Studio, make sure you select a correct gradle JDK from the IDE settings.

Had a call with [~accountid:712020:afce2c9f-c112-4254-8654-198da5ffe368] and [~accountid:6096595fb9ac3a007193a097] to discuss how the method currently works. 

The goal is given optimal UL and MP spend on city level decided in top down approach, figure out how to shuffle the MP budget across individual growth zones to achieve “liquidity”. Liquidity is a GMV target set by finance. MP budget acts as a constraint here, as it is not possible to assign each growth zone x% of city GMV as budget for MP spend.

Given the MP spend % on city level, forecasts on zone type level are created for various time horizons. The forecasted zone type level GMV is then assigned to individual zones proportional to historical GMV of the zones. Ultimately, which zone to prioritize is based on business logic (e.g. growth prime zones, see [this|https://docs.google.com/document/d/11jyyAMZiCEUQaraU_HCP0o_kEpqcdXrrp1reO31AJi4/edit?pli=1&tab=t.0#heading=h.e8hyitoi733d] framework).

One challenge here is the data quality of campaigns on zone type level. As a preliminary step, we agreed that we will do a deep dive and share results with [~accountid:712020:afce2c9f-c112-4254-8654-198da5ffe368] to see if modeling is even feasible.

thanks for the quick response! Here’s the input from the legal side: 

{color:#36b37e}+*Recommendation: AI agent-enabled manual scraping.*+{color}

Here’s how I rank the four options, from lowest to highest legal risk:

# *Manual scraping by Ops:* This carries the lowest legal risk.  That said, it would require significant manual effort, which I understand makes it impractical.
# *Third-party providers (e.g. Realytics):* Risk level is low to medium, depending on the contract. If we include appropriate indemnities and liability caps, legal exposure is manageable. The downside is technical, which limits the value of the data for our use case.
# *AI agent-enabled manual scraping:* Moderate legal risk overall, but if we follow key mitigation measures (single neutral user profile, low-frequency scraping, no persistent identifiers, no bypassing of access controls), this can be a well-balanced option. Operationally, it’s better than pure manual scraping and gives us access to full pricing data compared to Realytics. *Recommendation: This is the best option when balancing legal risk with operational benefit.*
# *Fully automated in-house scraping:* from a technical perspective, is fully automated more detectable than AI agent-enabled manual scraping?  In any case, this carries more legal risk. Courts and platforms are more likely to view full automation as deliberate, industrial-scale extraction, even if we scrape only with limitations. AI agent manual scraping can be more credibly framed as “human-supervised market research.”
If in-house automation is also _more_ detectable from a technical standpoint (e.g. triggering anti-bot systems), then I would recommend excluding it entirely from consideration at this stage.

{color:#ff5630}+*Legal risks and recommended mitigation measures:*+{color}

All of the risks related to scraping are highlighted in the [general guidance|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CXQTzhuvQVvJh67_9LJ4HDjPCSiK-8izo1AUapnGOz0/edit?tab=t.0], so risk mitigation measures from there should be kept in mind (i.e. no unethical scraping - overwhelming or compromising servers; no large-scale, high frequency, real-time scraping; only using the data for benchmarking). However, wanted to highlight the following as well as the bigger legal risks:

# *Terms of Service violation:* Accessing data behind a login likely breaches competitor platform terms, which could trigger cease-and-desist letters or monetary claims. *Mitigation:*
## Ensure scraping closely mimics normal user behaviour to reduce detection risk (e.g. human browsing patterns, session frequency, keep scraping low-frequency and low-volume)
## Document the purpose and limitations internally to demonstrate good faith and intent (e.g. for internal benchmarking, not commercial exploitation or real-time price-adjustments).
# *GDPR Compliance -* In the current MVP, we use a single neutral profile. Risk is low and likely outside the scope of GDPR. However, in future iterations, if we simulate multiple user profiles to test personalised pricing, we may begin processing pseudonymous personal data or engage in profiling under GDPR. *Mitigation:*
## For the current scope, maintain one static account, and collect only zone-based, non-identifying data.
## Before moving to any future version involving multiple accounts or behavioural variation, involve Privacy/Legal to assess data protection implications.

We are quite confident the charges the customer is referring to are related to this payment. 
[https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/3319159438|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/3319159438]

There was an authorization for 405 CZK (16.28 EUR)  and an authorization adjustment to 415.00 CZK (16.69 EUR). 

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount.

* 14 use cases ([link|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1DIlB96topLkGdcxpstPqmarLg4sD-n7p3HNif5KZaX8/edit?gid=0#gid=0]) use User Enrolled to Comms event as an Entry Schedule event, which means that these use cases are covered by Admin targeting.

Hello: 



# *Agreement between SIA AUTO and Taxi SIA*

I believe you meant _Taxi SIA_. If yes, then: it will sign an *Apkalpošanas līgums* (Service Agreement) with _SIA AUTO_ to manage and motivate the use of all leased cars under the _SIA AUTO_ fleet on the Bolt platform. These vehicles will operate under _Taxi SIA_ and, if needed, under additional legal entities such as _Taxi1 SIA_, _Taxi2 SIA_, etc.

In parallel, Bolt will have a *branding agreement* directly with _Taxi SIA_, under which all vehicles managed through the AUTO<–>Taxi SIA agreement will be eligible to earn bonuses. Bonus qualification will be tracked by *car VIN number*, meaning the bonus applies regardless of whether the car operates under Taxi SIA, Taxi1 SIA, or any other related entity.

----

# *Registration of Taxi SIA, Taxi1 SIA, etc., on the platform*

Yes, _Taxi SIA_ will act as the *main fleet*, managing the majority of vehicles.
_Taxi1 SIA_, _Taxi2 SIA_, and similar entities will be *side fleets*, each functioning as fully licensed transportation service providers under their own legal registration, providing ride-hailing services independently on the platform.

----

# *Vehicle holder on the license*

Yes, _Taxi1 SIA_, _Taxi2 SIA_, etc., must be listed as the *vehicle holders* on the vehicle registration documents. This is a legal requirement for them to obtain the necessary licenses and be activated on the Bolt platform.

----

# *Vehicle and order visibility in Bolt platform records*

Orders and vehicle activity will only be recorded under the fleet profile that provides the service — *vehicle ownership is not relevant* in this context.

Examples:

* If car *AA-0001* is rented out by _SIA AUTO_ but registered under _Taxi SIA_ as the holder, it will appear and operate exclusively under the _Taxi SIA_ profile in our app.
* If car *AA-0002* is rented out by _SIA AUTO_ but the holder is _Taxi1 SIA_, then all rides will be recorded under the _Taxi1 SIA_ company profile only. The _Taxi SIA_ will be only responsible for ensuring _Taxi1 SIA_ operates the vehicle (performance).
* If another vehicle is registered under _Taxi2 SIA_ (with all licenses obtained), it will be activated under that _Taxi2 SIA_ company profile alone, and all related data and earnings will be recorded accordingly in that company.

----

# *Nature of the service provided by SIA AUTO*

_SIA AUTO_ will *rent out* their leased vehicles individually to _Taxi SIA_, _Taxi1 SIA_, _Taxi2 SIA_, etc. Under the *_Apkalpošanas līgums_*, _Taxi SIA_ will be responsible for *maintaining the vehicles* and ensuring they are *actively used* on the Bolt platform within _Taxi SIA_ or _Taxi1 SIA_, _Taxi2 SIA_ etc. companies.

*🛡️ Full Analysis*

*Click to read*

h4. 1. Background and Context
*What is being done*
Bolt is expanding the scope of employee data collected for Diversity & Inclusion (D&I) purposes. The collection will include the following sensitive data categories:
* Ethnicity
* Sexual orientation
* Religion
* Disability
* Caregiver status
* Veteran status
* Migrant status
This data will be collected on a *voluntary* basis from employees and used primarily for *aggregated trend analysis* in OneModel. It is not intended for individual-level use.
*Why it is being done*
The key purposes are:
* ✅ Supporting *reasonable adjustments*
* ✅ Meeting *reporting obligations* (e.g., CSRD for disability)
* ✅ Designing inclusive People strategies and policies
* ✅ Performing demographic analysis to identify any systemic issues
*Where it is being done*
Initial rollout is focused on GDPR jurisdictions:
* United Kingdom
* Estonia
* Romania
* Germany
* Poland
----
h3. 2. Privacy Assessment
⚖️ *Lawful Basis*
Processing is based on *explicit consent* (GDPR Art. 9(2)(a)):
* ✅ Data is to be submitted voluntarily.
* 🔄 *Action*: We need to implement a consent mechanism within the chosen collection tool that is informed, explicit, and auditable.
📢 *Transparency and Notification*
* ✅ Bolt already has an employee privacy notice on Confluence.
* 🔄 *Action*: We will update the existing privacy notice to reflect:
** New data categories
** Voluntary nature of submission
** Purposes and systems involved (e.g., OneModel)
🔍 *Data Minimisation*
* 🔄 *Follow-up*: We need to confirm with stakeholders whether *all* D&I data points are necessary, or whether some categories (e.g., veteran or migrant status) could be excluded.
🌐 *International Data Transfers*
* ✅ OneModel is covered under a valid DPA with Bolt.
* 🔄 *Follow-up*: We need to verify whether *identifiable* sensitive data is being stored in OneModel.
** If so, *we* may need to update the DPA to reflect the inclusion of these data types.
----
h3. 3. Recommendations and Follow-Up Questions
💡 *Recommendations*
* Embed a consent mechanism directly into the data collection interface (Google Forms/Workday or equivalent).
* Limit access to raw data; ensure outputs are anonymised and aggregated.
🔄 *Follow-Up Questions*
# *Data Collection Mechanism*: What tool will be used for collection (Workday, Google Forms, etc.)?
# *Data Necessity*: Are all proposed categories necessary for the outcomes intended?
# *OneModel Storage Format*: Will any *identifiable* sensitive data be stored in OneModel?
